definition: Latent means present but hidden — really there, not yet showing itself, and capable of surfacing when conditions call it out.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word latent. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know latent should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The counter looked spotless until the technician dusted it for latent prints — marks laid down by a touch and unseen until the powder found them.
Potential is weaker than latent: a potential talent might not exist at all — mere room for one — while a latent talent is really there, lying quiet and waiting.
Incipient is stronger than latent: what is latent still lies wholly out of sight, while an incipient change has broken the surface and faintly begun to show.

Dormant means asleep — once active and able to wake again, like a volcano between eruptions or a club nobody has convened in years. Latent makes a different claim: the thing is genuinely there but has never yet shown itself at all.

Undeveloped says only that the growth hasn't happened — undeveloped land, an undeveloped backhand. Latent goes further: the thing already exists, real and complete enough to surface, needing only the conditions that will call it out.

Latere, 'to lie hidden,' mostly stayed hidden: English kept only latent and latency from it. Its one flourish is on the periodic table — lanthanum, named in 1839 for the way the element lay concealed inside another mineral for years, takes its name from the root's Greek cousin lanthanein, 'to escape notice.'
Latent means present but hidden — really there, not yet showing itself, and capable of surfacing when conditions call it out.
The infection can stay latent for a decade: carriers feel nothing, test clear on routine screens, and pass every physical — while the virus waits, whole and quiet, in the nerves.
Latent names exactly that interval.
The thing is fully present — not approaching, not developing, already there — yet nothing on the surface betrays it.
When symptoms finally arrive, nothing new has been added; what was hidden has simply stepped into view.
Latent is the laboratory's word for hiddenness — latent prints, latent infections, latent demand.
It differs from its neighbors by what it claims: a potential talent might not exist yet; a dormant one has shown itself before and sleeps; a latent one is really there and has never yet surfaced.
That 'really there' is the word's whole force — when the latent thing finally appears, nothing new has been created; something present all along has simply come into view.

Cleaning out her great-aunt's apartment, Nora found a shoebox of film rolls labeled 1968 — exposed, the notes said, but never processed.
A technician warned her the rolls might hold nothing.
Yet the images were there, latent in the emulsion: every frame her great-aunt had clicked was chemically recorded and complete, invisible only because nothing had ever called it out.
In the darkroom tray, fifty-year-old afternoons rose out of the blank film — a wedding, a protest, a kitchen full of strangers.
Nothing new was added in that red-lit room; what appeared had been present all along.
